create.title: One-sided persistence and exact local-moment bridge
create.statement_tex: Let P(t)=N(sqrt(t))-pi t with the inclusive integer-jump convention. For u>=0, P(x+u)>=P(x)-pi u and P(x-u)<=P(x)+pi u whenever x-u>=0. Thus a positive value persists to the right and a negative value to the left. If Q(Y,W) bounds every relevant length-W local square integral near x asymp Y and M=|P(x)|, then (M^2/4)min(W,M/(2pi))<=Q(Y,W), hence M<<Q^(1/3)+(Q/W)^(1/2). If W=Y^alpha, E=Y^(beta+o(1)), and Q<<WY^(1/2+delta)+E, then with q=max(alpha+1/2+delta,beta) the delivered exponent is max(q/3,(q-alpha)/2). In particular the standard local scale gives max(1/4,1/6+alpha/3); at fixed alpha=1/4+sigma it gives 1/4+sigma/3, while a strict quarter bound on a longer window requires total Q<<Y^(3/4+o(1)). Uniform unit-window L2 control is exponent-wise equivalent to uniform pointwise control. The accepted global moment alone does not imply the local supremum.
create.next_action: Use the exact two-branch formula for every future local-moment proposal. Do not suppress the cubic branch or infer a local supremum from a global average.

create.title: Integer-cell and one-separated density-one quarter theorem
create.statement_tex: For every integer n and n<=t<n+1, P(t)=P(n)-pi(t-n), so int_n^(n+1)P(t)^2dt=(P(n)-pi/2)^2+pi^2/12. For every one-separated set Xset in [Y,2Y], sign-oriented unit persistence intervals have bounded overlap and sum_(x in Xset)|P(x)|^2<<_epsilon Y^(3/2+epsilon). In particular sum_(Y<=n<=2Y)|P(n)|^2<<_epsilon Y^(3/2+epsilon), and for every eta>0 the number of integers n in [Y,2Y] with |P(n)|>Y^(1/4+eta) is <<_(epsilon,eta)Y^(1-2eta+epsilon). Also |P(t)|<=|P(n)|+pi on n<=t<n+1, so the uniform real theorem is equivalent up to O(1) to the theorem at every integer. This is a discrete density-one theorem and does not bound a prescribed integer.
create.next_action: Use this only for discrete exceptional counts and for reducing uniform real control to prescribed integers. It does not remove any individual exceptional integer.

create.title: Exact short-window triangular rational-frequency cluster kernel
create.statement_tex: For a fixed finite exponential polynomial S(t)=sum_lambda a_lambda e(lambda t), an interval I of length W and center c satisfies int_I|S(t)|^2dt<=(pi^2/4)W int_0^1 sum_nu |sum_(lambda in C_(nu,theta))a_lambda e(lambda c)|^2 dtheta, where C_(nu,theta)=[(nu+theta)/W,(nu+1+theta)/W). This is the exact sinc-square triangular form; equal frequencies are aggregated with all cross terms. The literal M1 frequencies are h/d and the literal M2 frequencies are h/(4d). On every window W<=Y^(1/2), the moving denominator prefix and each dyadic Vaaler height have O(1) changes, so all scales form O(log Y) fixed-symbol strata; floors, hard top, stars, both signs, chi_4, bottom, and R5 ownership are retained. At the accepted minimax block D=Y^(1/2),L=Y^(1/6), the frequency diameter is O(Y^(-1/3)). If W=Y^alpha with alpha<1/3, all frequencies occupy one random cell for measure 1-o(1), so the cluster form is >=(1-o(1))|S(c)|^2 and supplies no smoothing gain. The obstruction is only subcoherent; it does not cover 1/3<alpha<1/2.
create.next_action: Use the fixed kernel only as an exact reduction. The remaining input is signed cancellation within the actual rational cells, not the Fourier identity itself.

create.title: Non-subcoherent actual M1/M2 cluster local moment
create.statement_tex: Fix 1/3<alpha<1/2 and W=Y^alpha. For every center c asymp Y and every fixed-symbol stratum of every literal M1/M2 dyadic block, with M1 frequency h/d, M2 frequency h/(4d), actual Vaaler coefficient, chi_4 on its literal coordinate, both signs, floors, profiles, hard top and stars, prove int_0^1 sum_nu |sum_(lambda in C_(nu,theta))a_lambda(c)e(lambda c)|^2dtheta<<_epsilon Y^(1/2+epsilon), uniformly with logarithmic all-block assembly. Together with bottom and R5 owners this gives sup_(|I|=W)int_I|P(t)|^2dt<<_epsilon WY^(1/2+epsilon), and the persistence bridge gives P(X)<<_epsilon X^(1/6+alpha/3+epsilon)<X^(1/3+epsilon). At alpha<1/3 the minimax block is subcoherent and this estimate is already pointwise-hard; at alpha>=1/2 the standard local scale gives no improvement over one third. This candidate is a stepping-stone below one third, not the quarter target.
create.next_action: Attack a fixed alpha just below one half using the actual chi_4-weighted rational-cell square. Any proof must beat the Popov/Nowak additive Y-scale error and preserve the literal M1/M2 coefficient systems.

create.title: Popov 2024 local second-moment source audit
create.statement_tex: Popov 2024 Theorem 10(ii) defines E_2(T,H)=(2H)^(-1)int_(T-H)^(T+H)P(x)^2dx and proves E_2(T,H)<<sqrt(T)+T(log T)^2/H for H<=T/2. Thus total local mass is <<Hsqrt(T)+T(log T)^2. For H=T^alpha, alpha<=1/2, the additive term has exponent q=1; the exact persistence bridge gives max(1/3,(1-alpha)/2), exactly one third on 1/3<=alpha<=1/2 and worse below. Theorem 10(iii)-(iv) begins the fourth and sixth local moments at H>=T^(1/2). These theorems do not improve the accepted one-third exponent and do not estimate the actual M1/M2 rational clusters.
create.next_action: Keep this as a completed guardrail. A useful local theorem must remove a fixed power from the additive T-scale term or prove the actual signed cluster bound directly.

reject.reason: Fubini controls only the average over window positions. A monotone inclusive-jump spike model has global moment Y^(3/2) while a prescribed short window has much larger mass.
At W=Y^(1/4+sigma), Q<<WY^(1/2) gives exponent 1/4+sigma/3 through the cubic persistence branch. Strict quarter requires sigma=o(1) or total Q<<Y^(3/4+o(1)).
The minimax band is subcoherent only for alpha<1/3, while the sharp persistence bridge improves one third throughout alpha<1/2. The range 1/3<alpha<1/2 is genuinely open.
The literal M1 phase is e(hX/d), while M2 is e(hX/(4d)). A common frequency requires an explicit relabelling with the coefficient and support changed accordingly.
The triangular random-cell formula is an exact positive re-expression. It supplies no cancellation inside a cell and is pointwise-strength in the subcoherent minimax range.
